insights.headline: Gold down 26% from January's record ahead of Diwali; MCX bullion steadies as Fed-hike bets ease
insights.summary: Gold is down more than 26% from January's $5,595 record to around $4,100 — a reset arriving just as India's festival season ramps up. Titan's 21% jewellery growth and early NRI buying in Dubai's sub-Dh500 gold market signal demand is waking up. Softer US jobs data eased Fed-hike bets and a pausing dollar lifted bullion off two-month lows on MCX, but elevated Treasury yields capped gains ahead of the Oct 27–28 FOMC meeting. Brokerages expect silver's five-year deficit to narrow into a 2027 surplus, keeping prices consolidating.

trending.title: Diwali window opens on the dip
trending.summary: Gold's 26% slide from January highs coincides with peak festive buying; Titan's 21% jewellery growth and early NRI buying in Dubai point to a demand revival.

trending.title: Fed repricing steadies MCX bullion
trending.summary: Weak US jobs data pushed October hike bets off the table, lifting MCX gold toward ₹1.49 lakh and silver toward ₹2.26 lakh/kg; FOMC minutes and the Oct 27–28 meeting set the next test.

trending.title: Silver supply turns: deficit to 2027 surplus
trending.summary: Brokerages see silver's deficit narrowing into surplus by 2027 — a structural turn arguing for price consolidation around current levels; technically silver is building a base above $60.

trending.title: Yields remain the ceiling
trending.summary: Long-dated Treasury yields near multi-decade highs keep a lid on gold's recovery; MCX gold slipped ₹160/10g as rate pressure persisted.

items.title: Gold corrects 26% from January record high — is this a buying opportunity ahead of Diwali?
items.summary: Gold is down more than 26% from its January record of $5,595 an ounce to around $4,100, pressured by multi-decade-high US Treasury yields and a firm dollar; analysts at Kotak Securities, Choice Broking and Tata Mutual Fund say valuations have turned more attractive and the festive/Diwali season could offer an entry window.

items.title: Silver may enter surplus by 2027 from supply deficit; brokerages see prices consolidating
items.summary: Brokerages expect silver's long-running supply deficit to narrow through 2026 and the market to flip into surplus by 2027, which should keep prices consolidating rather than extending the rally; 12-month brokerage targets on MCX sit around ₹3.5–4 lakh per kg, CNBC-TV18 reports.

items.title: Gold, Silver Edge Higher On MCX As Fed Rate-Hike Bets Ease
items.summary: Bullion edged higher on MCX after softer US jobs data eased October Fed rate-hike bets; December gold futures traded around ₹1,49,212 per 10 grams and December silver near ₹2,26,322 per kg by mid-afternoon, though elevated Treasury yields capped gains ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting.

items.title: Titan Q2FY27 update: Consumer businesses grow 25% YoY, jewellery up 21%
items.summary: Titan's consumer businesses grew 25% year-on-year in Q2FY27 excluding bullion, with jewellery up 21%, watches 30%, EyeCare 28% and international business 97%; the company added 78 net stores, a strong signal of jewellery demand heading into the festive season.

items.title: Gold, silver prices rise as yields ease but December Fed risk remains
items.summary: Spot gold and silver rose in early US trading as long-dated Treasury yields eased; US data was mixed — September payrolls added just 29,000 while the ISM services PMI hit its highest since July 2022 — and Fed-funds pricing now leans toward no change at the December meeting.

items.title: Gold rebounds from two-month lows as US Dollar, Treasury yields retreat
items.summary: Gold bounced off a two-month low near $4,100 as the dollar's rally paused, but elevated bond yields and geopolitical risk — including reports of Israel preparing a potential strike on Iran — kept a lid on gains ahead of Wednesday's FOMC minutes.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD builds base above $60, eyes $64
items.summary: Silver is building a base above $60, up over 1% to $61.13 after bouncing off $60.36 lows, FXStreet's technical desk notes; a break above $62 opens the way toward $64–65 resistance, while a drop below the Oct 2 low of $59.69 would turn the short-term bias bearish.

items.title: Dubai gold prices drop further ahead of Indian festivals Navratri, Diwali
items.summary: Dubai gold slipped further on Tuesday, with 24K at Dh496.75 a gram at the open — below Dh500 — prompting early festive buying by NRI families ahead of Navratri and Diwali; Pepperstone's Chris Weston says the short-term investment case for gold remains weak.

items.title: Gold price today, October 6, 2026: 24K rate slips ₹160 per 10 gm from Monday
items.summary: Gold edged lower on Tuesday, with 24K (99.9% purity) at ₹14,902 a gram in most cities — down ₹16 a gram, or ₹160 per 10 grams, from Monday — a milder decline than Monday's ₹1,100-per-10-gram drop.

items.title: World Bank flags oil, El Niño and global market risks to growth
items.summary: The World Bank warned that oil-price swings, El Niño disruptions and financial-market stress are the key risks to global growth — a combination that typically supports gold's safe-haven role even as it dents demand elsewhere.
